newsitem.title: ITALY: Ex-wife held in Gucci murder probe - police.
newsitem.headline: Ex-wife held in Gucci murder probe - police.

text.p: Five people were arrested on Friday in connection with the 1995 murder of Italian fashion king Maurizio Gucci, including his first wife, police said.
"We confirm that we arrested Patrizia Reggiani Martinelli this morning on suspicion of involvement in the killing," a police official told Reuters.

Legal sources said police alleged that Gucci's 49-year-old first wife commissioned the fatal shooting, one of the most mysterious recent killings in Italy. Gucci's former wife was arrested in an apartment in central Milan.
Four other people -- a woman who was identified by Italian news agencies as her spiritual adviser, and three men -- were also arrested on the orders of Milan prosecutor Carlo Nocerino.
Nocerino was not immediately available for comment. His office said he expected to question the detainees later.
Gucci, 45, the last grandson of Guccio Gucci who founded the international fashion dynasty, was shot dead in broad daylight outside his office in Milan in March, 1995.

Police said the attack was carried out by a well-dressed assassin who they believed used a pistol with a silencer. Investigating magistrates had been pursuing Gucci's business affairs in Switzerland to try to find a motive for the murder.

Gucci had been head of the luxury leather goods and fashion empire but had sold his 50 percent stake two years before his death, ending the feuding family's involvement in a business that became a byword for elegance and status.
A millionaire, he had recently set up his own tourism business called Vierse.
Gucci, known the world over for its red and green motif and linked GG gilt logo, appeared on thousands of products in the 1980s that became de rigeur for the international jet-set.
The company grew from humble origins in a saddlery shop in Florence in 1906. It is now publicly traded on the Amsterdam and New York stock markets.
